name: Barking Deer Foraging Sites
description: Barking deer forage-site habitats vs. available land proportions (Hainan Island). Strong preference. IMS Ch. 16 (goodness-of-fit).
studyDescription: Researchers recorded the habitat at 426 sites where barking deer were observed foraging on Hainan Island, China. The available land is 4.8% woods, 14.7% cultivated grassplot, 39.6% deciduous forest, and 40.9% other. The goodness-of-fit test asks whether the deer forage in proportion to habitat availability or prefer certain habitats.

variableDescriptions.habitat: The habitat type of a barking-deer forage site: woods, cultivated grassplot, deciduous forest, or other.

sourceDetail: OpenIntro / IMS Ch. 16. Barking deer microhabitat study, Hainan Island, China. Observed 4/16/61/345 vs. land proportions 0.048/0.147/0.396/0.409. χ² = 284.1, df = 3, p ≈ 0 — the deer strongly prefer certain habitats (far more foraging in "Other" than availability predicts).
